item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Contrary to the above, this doesn't work for me because it feels like it comes from a time where articles had to be super-squicky and horrifying to work. I know most people enjoy this bit, but I absolutely do not:

While SCP-352 prefers any type of human flesh over any other type of meat, it appears to have a special propensity for children between 0 and 2 years of age. After observation of highly elevated levels of co-operation and a reduced tendency to attack staff while consuming flesh of this type, a possible alteration in the current diet is being considered.

For me, it absolutely kills the enjoyment of the article I had up to then, as it's way over-the-top spoopy and evil of the Foundation. "Foundation is evil" can work, but it doesn't in this case.

So I just read 353 and downvoted it, and I see some comparisons here, so I wanted to take a second and note why this skip works and "Vector" doesn't.

  • Not a teenager.
  • No supervillain name.
  • Based off established mythology.
  • Considerably more otherworldly, and thus scarier. (353 is scary, but it's not communicated well in the article.)
  • Classic "Foundation is evil" twist at the end. I like it, fight me.

Yeah. Definitely prefer Baba Yaga here.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I see this as a Euclid. The comparison to 106 doesn't really hold up, either, because that one pretty regularly attempts to break containment, and does a lot of damage that is pretty much always needing to be repaired. We lock this one up and toss a cow in through a hatch periodically, and it's contained. If it was roaming free, I'd agree with Keter, but I'm not seeing a good justification for it now.

I also don't like the baby eating thing. I don't see what could be gained by giving 352 human flesh, let alone babies specifically, so it just feels like one of those "giving them what they want" sort of things, though it's currently just "under consideration" and not actually implemented.

-1 for now, but if the Class is changed, and if something is added, like the Site Director or the Ethics Committee replying to the addendum saying nothing valuable could be gained from stepping over that moral line, I'd switch to an upvote.

+ Something like this, maybe?
– hide block

"SCP-352 says it will cooperate with us if we give it babies/toddlers to eat. 352 is an anomalous object, and its cooperation is not required in order to contain it. The Foundation does many horrible things to protect the world, but catering to every whim humanoid SCPs may have is not one of those things, unless doing so furthers the primary goals of the Foundation in securing, containing, and protecting, none of which would be accomplished by fulfilling this particular request. It is the unanimous decision of the Ethics Committee at this time to decline SCP-352's request. If new information comes to light, the Ethics Committee will review this decision and act accordingly.

Signed,
Foundation Ethics Committee
<insert black boxes here>"

Now, this is in the triple digits, and it's an old one, so I don't expect it will change, but something indicating that the "consideration" was rejected would be good, imo. Cold, not cruel, etc. Humanoid scip requests are supposed to be largely denied if fulfilling them won't really profit the Foundation anything, right? It just seems to me like an added thing to increase squick or something.

I'll remove my downvote if it's at least changed to Euclid, but I'd need to see both those things added/updated to change to an upvote.

Now, after all that, I like the scip itself. Object Class and that last bit are really my only gripes. Good work.

item.title: Statistics
item.content:encoded:
I'm not a fan of "nearly all cases" type odds, such as:

Bites from SCP-352 lead to high exposure in 99.9% of cases.

because it implies that at a minimum they let her bite 1000 people to establish that percentage. It'd be much more reasonable to say "In 100% of known cases" or "In all but one case", or in only █ out of ███ cases did the victim recover. I know 99.9% of people won't be bugged by something like this, but I'm a math guy.
